title: Edge surge and fallbacks rollforward plan - Nov 2025 (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for the Nov 2025 rollforward targeting edge routing changes, region surge policy tweaks, and a new fallthrough fallback behavior. Goal: ship with a low-risk canary, validate traffic shaping (edge region weighting), and confirm automatic fallbacks across Dedicated and Hosted tiers. Not a final runbook — use as the source of truth for the rollout window and post-release notes.

TL;DR (one-paragraph):
We will deploy edge-routing v2 to all clusters on 2025-11-12 during the 02:00-06:00 UTC window with a three-stage rollout: internal canary (5% traffic) -> regional canaries (per-region 5-15%) -> global ramp to 100%. The deployment includes: new surge-throttle policy (edge-surge v2), deterministic fallthrough routing when a model variant is unavailable, and metrics labels to capture cross-region latency breakdowns. Rollback criteria are defined below. Primary risk: higher p99 tail latency for small-sequence chat requests in APAC under heavy small-batch traffic.

Preflight checklist (complete before 2025-11-12 00:00 UTC):
- [ ] Confirm CI green on runtime PR and integration tests (PR #8742)
- [ ] Smoke build pushed to staging images repo with tag edge-surge-v2-canary
- [ ] Load test summary uploaded to Confluence (link in linked_artifacts) with baseline comparisons (latency/cost)
- [ ] Capacity reservation for Dedicated pools confirmed with infra and billing (ticket RL-4539)
- [ ] Observability: new metric labels enabled (region, route_type, fallback_reason) and dashboards published
- [ ] Alerting: set temporary thresholds for new metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate) in Sentry/Datadog
- [ ] Communication: notify customer-success and oncall rotation for the window, post to #release-ops and #oncall 24 hours before
- [ ] Feature flag created: feature.edge_surge_v2 (default OFF) with per-tenant targeting
- [ ] Rollout runbook printed/available to oncall (this doc)

Rollout calendar (UTC) — 2025-11-12:
- 00:00 — Quiet hours start, freeze non-release merges for runtime repo
- 01:00 — Final verification of monitoring and alert contact lists
- 02:00 — Deploy canary image to internal-only clusters (tag: canary-internal-20251112)
- 02:10 — Run smoke tests (automated): /health, small chat, embeddings sample, KV cache warmup
- 02:25 — Manual verification by SRE on duty: dashboards, traces for 10 sample requests
- 02:45 — If stable, enable feature.edge_surge_v2 for internal orgs (5% global traffic)
- 03:30 — Evaluate metrics for 30 minutes; if passing, enable per-region canaries: EU (10%), NA (10%), APAC (5%)
- 04:30 — Monitoring window: observe regional error rates and latency; check cost delta telemetry
- 05:00 — If no regressions, ramp to 50% global for 30 minutes, then 100% after approval
- 05:45 — Final verification, post-release announce to #release-ops
- 06:00 — End window; begin 6-hour high-watch period (oncall continue monitoring)

Canary success criteria (must be met to progress):
- Error-rate (4xx/5xx) increase <= 0.25 percentage points absolute vs baseline for canary buckets
- p99 latency change <= +25% relative or absolute delta <= 120ms (whichever is smaller)
- No increase in model-availability fallbacks > 1% of requests in the canary buckets
- No unexplained increase in cost-per-token > 10% for the canary traffic
- SRE signoff in the Slack thread (min two approvals: SRE+Release Eng)

Automated checks & smoke scripts (commands for SRE):
- Smoke (HTTP): curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-chat","input":"hello"}'
- Embedding sanity: python tools/embedding_check.py --key $SMOKE_KEY --model rwd-embed-1 --count 20
- KV warmup: kubectl exec -n runtime deploy/edge-proxy -- /opt/bin/kv_warmup --region eu-west-1
- Canary metrics quick-check: datadog query "avg:last_5m:runtime.request.p99{env:staging,canary:true} by {region}"

Rollback plan (if any of the hardcore triggers fire):
Hard triggers (immediate rollback to last-known-good):
- Global error-rate delta > 1.5 percentage points for > 5m in any production region
- Sustained p99 latency increase > 250ms for > 5m in any Dedicated pool (risk to SLAs)
- Model availability fallback spikes > 5% sustained for > 10m
- Critical customer-reported failures for Tier 1 customers (as reported to CS or SRE)

Rollback steps (fast):
1) Flip feature flag feature.edge_surge_v2 -> OFF via LaunchDarkly (or internal flag UI)
2) Scale edge-proxy deployment to previous image tag (kubectl set image deployment/edge-proxy edge-proxy=image@sha256:<prev>)
3) If rollback fails or is slow, activate emergency fallback route: set-policy edge-route priority=legacy via routing-admin
4) Post incident note to #oncall with rollback reason and immediate steps

Fallback behavior notes (what changed):
- New deterministic fallthrough: if variant X is missing, route to variant Y with explicit cost-based penalty. This reduces N+1 requests but may alter per-token cost distribution.
- Telemetry includes fallback_reason label now; use datadog tag "fallback_reason:" for queries
- Paper trail: any fallthrough event should spawn an incident in RL-4539 if rate > 1%

Observability runbook (where to look):
- Dashboards: Edge Routing Overview (prod + staging), Model Availability by Variant, Per-region Latency Heatmap
- Traces: sample failed request traces in Tempo/Jaeger under service=runtime-edge
- Logs: correlate 429/503 with upstream saturation in the edge-proxy logs (index: runtime-edge-logs)
- Alerts: temporary thresholds set under "Edge Surges (Nov 2025)" in Datadog

Communications and escalation:
- Primary channel: #release-ops (public), fallback: #oncall (private, paging)
- Customer Success: ping cs-oncall and tier-1 CSAs 15 minutes before ramp to 100%
- Exec update: short note to execs if rollback occurs or if any Tier 1 customer alerts

Post-release checklist and notes (first-pass for release notes):
- [ ] Collect canary vs baseline metrics and paste into Confluence summary (include graphs)
- [ ] Draft release notes (see below) and circulate to Product/CS for 24h review
- [ ] Open a follow-up ticket to track any region-specific tweaks (assign to infra)
- [ ] Schedule a 30-minute retro within 72 hours with SRE, Release Eng, and Product

Draft release notes (to be edited into final changelog):
- Edge routing: introduce edge-surge v2 policy with improved regional surge throttling and deterministic fallthroughs to improve availability during sudden traffic spikes.
- New telemetry: per-request labels for region, route_type, and fallback_reason are now populated in traces and metrics. This enables quicker root-cause analysis of cross-region issues.
- Config: new feature flag feature.edge_surge_v2 to toggle behavior per-org for staged rollouts.
- Known limitations: APAC small-batch latency may see transient p99 increases when under high small-sequence chat load; mitigations are in progress (RL-4611).

Known risks and mitigations (open items):
- Risk: bursty multi-tenant small-batch traffic increasing p99 tails in APAC. Mitigation: hold APAC at lower canary percentage and run targeted load tests with mix of seq lengths.
- Risk: cost shift due to fallthrough routing sending requests to warmer but more expensive variants. Mitigation: monitor cost-per-token and surface top 10 tenants affected to finops.

Retro prompts (what to capture after the release):
- Did the canary criteria adequately protect SLA customers? If not, which criteria were insufficient?
- Any silent failures that alerts did not catch? Update alerts accordingly.
- Was communication cadence sufficient for CS and Platform teams?
- Time-to-rollback: measure and see if automation can shorten it.

Notes to self (TODOs before finalizing):
- Add contact phone/pager numbers for oncall rotation into the header
- Attach load test artifact and raw logs to Confluence page
- Confirm whether any enterprise customers require private notification before ramp to 100%

Appendix: quick run commands and dashboards
- Enable flag (LD): curl -X PATCH https://launchdarkly.internal/api/flags/feature.edge_surge_v2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $LD_TOKEN' -d '{"on":true,"targets":[{"values":["internal-org"],"variation":true}]}'
- Revert image: kubectl -n prod set image deploy/edge-proxy edge-proxy=registry.redwood.ai/edge-proxy:stable-20251021
- Datadog query examples: "sum:last_5m:runtime.requests{feature:edge_surge_v2,env:prod} by {region}"

-- End of draft --

Author note: keeping this intentionally pragmatic and checklist-driven. Expect edits from SRE and infra owners; will lock a final runbook once a successful staging pass completes.
